digest:
## V5-3 core task
Implement pure `compute_lazy_marks` + `compute_block_reward` per RFC 0012 v2 / RFC 0019; integrate touch on all state transitions; wire dynamic reward in `Chain::seal`.

## Post-V5-2 gaps
- `state.rs`: uses `DEF_BLOCKS_PER_HOUR`, no `marks_per_coin_per_hour`, no `satur_hours` pre-clamp; touch only on Stake/Unstake (+ INIT cursor set).
- Missing touch: Transfer (sender+recipient), BurnMark, PolicyTx.
- `chain.rs`: fixed `block_reward` + legacy `season_ppm(ts)`; no `base_emission_per_block` formula.
- No `marks.rs`/`economics.rs`; no `inflation_*` tests.

## Suggested slices
1. pure fns + unit tests
2. state touch refactor
3. chain seal + dev defaults

## Out of scope
V5-4 deferred policies, V5-5 ClaimIPv4Batch apply, V5-6 TUI, V5-7 CLI.

Legacy policy_ver==1 seal path: keep separate branch or unify under compute_block_reward for all configs.
Rust field rename marks_per_hour → marks_per_coin_per_hour: optional slice4 or defer.
warnings: CQDS start_grep skipped to minimize round-trips; discovery via local rg on crates/pwm-core/src.
RFC 0019 names legacy_block_reward but GenCfg V5-2 only has block_reward — document maps block_reward as practical fallback.
